questions.help: 7 Seat belts 7.1 Purpose and effectivenessThe purpose of a seat belt is to retain and protect the driver and occupants in the event of sudden stopping, collision or the vehicle rolling over. The seat belt prevents the occupants of a vehicle from being catapulted out of it and absorbs part of the energy of an impact.During a frontal collision against an indeformable object, a vehicle stops in a tenth of a second, but due to inertia, the occupants will continue moving at the same speed as the vehicle was travelling at. Therefore, there is the likelihood of colliding with the steering wheel or the windshield, which will result in serious injuries being sustained.To avoid this, the seat belt slows the movement of the body by stretching out, as if is made of an elastic material, by an extensible action.(Página 75 del manual 'Learning to drive')7 Seat belts                 7.6 Misconceptions of safety belts"In town, a seat belt is not necessary, as the speed is low”At only 30 or 40 kilometres per hour an accident can be fatal if the head hits the sun visor, dash board or steering wheel.In an impact at low-speed, the safety belt will normally ensure that the occupants escape unhurt or suffer minor injury.     "In short journeys seat belts aren’tneeded”Most accidents involving casualties occur within a few kilometres from the place of departure, so it’s important to use seat belts on all journeys.(Página 78 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: 10 Head restraints  Head restraints are very effective in the event of a collision, avoiding or reducing the severity of injuries to the neck or vertebrates caused by the sudden movement, forward and back, of the head (whiplash). It is therefore imperative to properly use them, both in front and back seats. Whiplash occurs when a person’s head moves backward and then forward suddenly with great force. Where there is doubt between two sizes, it is important to choose the one that is more fitted and can be adjusted correctly, since the interior padding usually stretches a little with use. If the rider wears glasses, it is important to try these with the helmet too.(Página 81 del manual 'Learning to drive')11 Crash helmets   11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmetApproval:Approval is the guarantee of quality, so it is important to be wary of helmets that have not been properly approved. If a helmet does not have a label of approval, it is because it has not successfully passed some tests to ensure minimum safety, and therefore its effectiveness is unknown.The structure of the helmet can be damaged without being externally noticed. If a blow to a helmet is received, possibly during a collision or, the helmet is even simply dropped from a height of more than 1.50 metres, it should be changed as soon as possible.(Página 82 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: 11 Crash helmets   11.1 Tips for buying a crash helmet Visors:Visors are strongly recommended. However, it is important to ensure that these do not mist up; therefore, special covers are available that increase the anti-mist properties. When the helmet does not include eye protection it is highly recommended that safety glasses are used, although this use is not mandatory. Without eye protection, there is obviously the risk that something may enter the eye (an insect, a particle of sand or dust, etc.,) which may cause the rider to become distracted; however, the cold and/or the wind constantly in the eyes also increases visual fatigue.(Página 82 del manual 'Learning to drive')
